svg.title: Amplitude of a driven oscillator versus driving frequency
svg.desc: Amplitude X of the same oscillator, with natural frequency f0, as a function of the driving frequency f, for small, medium and heavy damping. Each curve peaks at resonance, when the driving frequency is close to f0. The less the damping, the taller and narrower the peak; double arrows show each curve’s width at half its height. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: The steady response grows near resonance and shrinks with damping
Five separately settled states of x″ + b x′ + x = cos(rt). Each advances 2π/ω0 model seconds; the
phase clock resets between examples. Settling transients are omitted.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
